content:
anya: FYI I found a flaky failure in our sample app when someone imports AsyncClient at module import time. app crashes on startup with RuntimeError.
kevin: Can you paste the minimal repro?
anya: yep, super small. gist: 3 files, main.py imports client from lib, lib.py creates AsyncClient at top-level.
anya: ```python
# lib.py
from redwood_sdk import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()  # created at import

# main.py
import lib  # triggers client creation
import asyncio

async def ping():
    await lib.client.get("https://example.com")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    asyncio.run(ping())
```
anya: log: ``RuntimeError: no running event loop`` when running under uvicorn or when using uvloop loop policy.
kevin: ah classic. AsyncClient (httpx) constructs some background tasks / uses `asyncio.get_running_loop()` internally, so creating it at import time is risky.
mohammed: also worth noting: if the app (or framework) sets a custom event loop policy (uvloop) after imports, or uses threads with thread-local loop, import-time creation ends up bound to wrong loop or none. we saw this when mixing `asyncio.run` + `loop.set_event_loop_policy` earlier.
anya: interestingly, it only fails intermittently — sometimes it logs fine and background refresh token tasks start; other times the process crashes.
kevin: intermittent -> race: depending on whether a loop is running when the client tries to create an internal task. If `AsyncClient()` calls `asyncio.get_running_loop()` at init it will raise outside coroutine. If it defers to `get_event_loop()` it might return a loop bound to current thread or policy, still brittle.
anya: repros show two variants: (1) plain `python main.py` using CPython builtin loop -> sometimes ok. (2) `uvicorn main:app --loop uvloop` -> crashes reliably.
kevin: quick mitigation: switch to lazy factory + context manager. e.g.:
```python
# lib.py
from typing import Optional
_client: Optional[AsyncClient] = None

def get_client() -> AsyncClient:
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        _client = AsyncClient()
    return _client
```
# use inside coroutines: `client = get_client()`
```
kevin: or even better, an async initializer: `async def init_client(): global _client; _client = AsyncClient(); await _client.startup()` that app calls from its startup hook.
anya: I tried lazy edge — it reduced crashes but didn't fully fix token refresh background task creation ordering under gunicorn + uvicorn workers.
mohammed: sounds like we need SDK change: Detect import-time init and warn in logs, or internally avoid creating tasks until the first async call. Feature request: Add `defer_startup=True` option so AsyncClient won't spawn background tasks in __init__.
kevin: Agreed. Also request: better typing for the factory pattern so mypy can catch accidental top-level initialization. e.g. `AsyncClientFactory[ClientType]` or `DeferredAsyncClient` class.
anya: filing a GH issue now with repro and annotated logs, putting a short test that runs under uvloop to reproduce.
ci-bot: CI check started for #3459 (anya/async-client-eager-import) :eyes:
anya: created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/3459 with repro and suggested patch.
kevin: thanks. next steps: we should (1) add defensive warning in docs about not creating AsyncClient at import time, (2) add `defer_startup` param and a `startup()` coroutine, (3) add an automated test matrix: {uvloop, asyncio} x {asyncio.run, uvicorn}.
mohammed: also add a lint rule in our sample apps repo to fail CI if AsyncClient() appears at module top-level. trivial grep.
anya: good idea, will open PR to sample-apps to add that grep check.
kevin: also add a short note in quickstart: "If you must create at import time, use `defer_startup=True` and call `await client.startup()` in your app startup hook."
anya: tagging @devx to track docs + SDK fix. :pray:
ci-bot: created task redwood/sdks#task-768 for followups.
